## Objective

Find either a smaller protein panel with comparable classification performance
or an alternative panel with improved performance. Compare it with the
in-class t-test/random-forest intersection followed by logistic regression.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(randomForest)
library(modelr)

load("../../data/biomarker-clean.RData")
```

## Reserving a test set

```{r split}
set.seed(101422)

part4_split <- initial_split(
  biomarker_clean,
  prop = 0.8,
  strata = group
)

part4_train <- training(part4_split)
part4_test <- testing(part4_split)

part4_train %>% count(group)
```

## 3. Establishing baseline from part 3

```{r}
source("part4baseline.R")
```


## 4. Using training-only to select our new smaller protein panel
```{r}
protein_names <- setdiff(
  names(part4_train),
  c("group", "ados")
)

part4_ranking <- purrr::map_dfr(protein_names, function(protein) {

  result <- t.test(
    part4_train[[protein]][part4_train$group == "ASD"],
    part4_train[[protein]][part4_train$group == "TD"]
  )

  tibble(
    protein = protein,
    p_value = result$p.value
  )
}) %>%
  arrange(p_value)
# choosing our proteins to start cross-validating
part4_ranking %>%
  slice_head(n = 3)
```
## 5. Using the top 3 proteins in cross validation
```{r}
set.seed(101422)

part4_folds <- vfold_cv(
  part4_train,
  v = 5,
  strata = group
)

evaluate_fold <- function(split) {

  fold_train <- analysis(split)
  fold_valid <- assessment(split)

  ranking <- purrr::map_dfr(protein_names, function(protein) {

    result <- t.test(
      fold_train[[protein]][fold_train$group == "ASD"],
      fold_train[[protein]][fold_train$group == "TD"]
    )

    tibble(
      protein = protein,
      p_value = result$p.value
    )
  }) %>%
    arrange(p_value)

  purrr::map_dfr(1:3, function(k) {

    selected <- head(ranking$protein, k)

    model_data <- fold_train %>%
      select(all_of(selected)) %>%
      mutate(class = fold_train$group == "ASD")

    model <- glm(
      class ~ .,
      data = model_data,
      family = binomial()
    )

    probabilities <- predict(
      model,
      newdata = fold_valid,
      type = "response"
    )

    tibble(
      panel_size = k,
      accuracy = mean(
        (probabilities > 0.5) == (fold_valid$group == "ASD")
      )
    )
  })
}

part4_cv_results <- part4_folds %>%
  mutate(scores = purrr::map(splits, evaluate_fold)) %>%
  select(id, scores) %>%
  unnest(scores)

part4_cv_summary <- part4_cv_results %>%
  group_by(panel_size) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_accuracy = mean(accuracy),
    sd_accuracy = sd(accuracy),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

part4_cv_summary
```

### Elijah Ret part
## 6. Select the best panel size
```{r}

part4_best <- part4_cv_summary %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_accuracy), panel_size) %>%
  slice(1)

part4_best

best_k <- part4_best$panel_size

best_proteins <- part4_ranking %>%
  slice_head(n = best_k) %>%
  pull(protein)

best_proteins
```

## 7. Fit the final model using the training set

```{r}
final_train <- part4_train %>%
  select(all_of(best_proteins)) %>%
  mutate(
    class = factor(part4_train$group, levels = c("TD", "ASD"))
  )

final_model <- glm(
  class ~ .,
  data = final_train,
  family = binomial()
)
```

## 8. Evaluate on the held-out test set

```{r}
test_probabilities <- predict(
  final_model,
  newdata = part4_test %>% select(all_of(best_proteins)),
  type = "response"
)

test_predictions <- factor(
  ifelse(test_probabilities > 0.5, "ASD", "TD"),
  levels = c("TD", "ASD")
)

part4_test_results <- tibble(
  truth = factor(part4_test$group, levels = c("TD", "ASD")),
  estimate = test_predictions
)

part4_test_results %>%
  accuracy(truth, estimate)

part4_test_results %>%
  conf_mat(truth, estimate)
```

## 9. Compare accuracy across panel sizes
```{r}

ggplot(
  part4_cv_summary,
  aes(x = panel_size, y = mean_accuracy)
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = pmax(0, mean_accuracy - sd_accuracy),
      ymax = pmin(1, mean_accuracy + sd_accuracy)
    ),
    width = 0.2
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Cross-validated accuracy by protein panel size",
    x = "Number of proteins",
    y = "Mean cross-validation accuracy"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 10. Summarize the selected panel
```{r}
tibble(
  panel_size = length(best_proteins),
  proteins = paste(best_proteins, collapse = ", "),
  cv_mean_accuracy = part4_best$mean_accuracy,
  cv_sd_accuracy = part4_best$sd_accuracy,
  test_accuracy = accuracy(
    part4_test_results,
    truth,
    estimate
  )$.estimate
)
```

## 11. Compare the alternative with the baseline


```{r baseline-comparison}
alternative_metrics <- part4_test_results %>%
  mutate(prob_asd = test_probabilities) %>%
  class_metrics(
    truth = truth,
    estimate = estimate,
    prob_asd,
    event_level = "second"
  )

part4_comparison <- bind_rows(
  baseline %>%
    mutate(
      model = "Baseline: t-test + random forest intersection",
      panel_size = length(proteins_sstar_question3)
    ),
  alternative_metrics %>%
    mutate(
      model = "Alternative: t-test only",
      panel_size = length(best_proteins)
    )
) %>%
  select(model, panel_size, .metric, .estimate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = .metric, values_from = .estimate)

knitr::kable(
  part4_comparison,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Held-out test performance (proportions from 0 to 1)"
)

baseline_accuracy <- baseline %>%
  filter(.metric == "accuracy") %>%
  pull(.estimate)

alternative_accuracy <- alternative_metrics %>%
  filter(.metric == "accuracy") %>%
  pull(.estimate)

accuracy_difference_pp <- 100 * (alternative_accuracy - baseline_accuracy)
protein_reduction <- length(proteins_sstar_question3) - length(best_proteins)
```
